pr_title: Retire one-time archive-orphan lane after Foundry VCS cutover
lens: P9 no-sprawl + DOC-CATALOG + doc class shape + thin-gateway pattern

verification_summary.governance_lanes_index_format: row retained with status=retired, kernel/runner/CI cells set to 'retired'

findings.title: ADR-0118 missing from docs/DOC-CATALOG.md
findings.evidence: git show 59534679:docs/DOC-CATALOG.md | grep -c ADR-0118 → 0 hits. Neighbors ADR-0115/0116/0117 are also absent, indicating systemic catalog drift unaddressed since PR #12.
findings.impact: Violates DOC-CATALOG single-source-of-truth invariant; doc-catalog fitness lane cannot route to ADR-0118; new agents cannot discover the retirement decision via canonical index.
findings.fix: Add ADR-0118 entry to docs/DOC-CATALOG.md under the ADR section with class=decision, status=Accepted, date=2026-05-16, supersedes=ADR-0052. Backfill ADR-0115/0116/0117 in same patch.

findings.title: ADR-0118 missing from docs/ADR-INDEX.md
findings.evidence: git show 59534679:docs/ADR-INDEX.md | grep -c ADR-0118 → 0 hits. Neighbors ADR-0115/0116/0117 also absent — same drift pattern as A2 finding on PR #12.
findings.impact: ADR-INDEX is the canonical decision-chain navigator; missing entries break traceability (supersedes ADR-0052), break adr-index fitness lane expectations, and prevent agents from locating retirement decisions.
findings.fix: Append ADR-0118 row to docs/ADR-INDEX.md with id, title, status=Accepted, date=2026-05-16, supersedes=[ADR-0052], related=[ADR-0116, ADR-0110..0113]. Backfill 0115/0116/0117.

findings.title: ADR-0118 missing from docs/machine-readable/decisions.json
findings.impact: Machine-readable decisions corpus diverges from authored ADR set; downstream tooling (Foundry agentic queries, RAG retrieval, supersedes-chain validators) cannot see ADR-0118; supersedes relationship to ADR-0052 is invisible to automation.
findings.fix: Add ADR-0118 object to docs/machine-readable/decisions.json with id, status, date, deciders, supersedes, related, owner. Re-run any decisions.json regeneration script if one exists.

findings.title: Amended ADRs lack explicit 'Amended by' annotation
findings.evidence: ADR-0104 diff replaces inline reference text only (`'Mechanical-prevention candidate landed separately as oya-governance-adapter-with-no-importer-kernel; do not extend the retired archive-orphan lane (ADR-0118).'`). ADR-0107 diff edits three table cells inline. Neither ADR adds a top-level `Amended by: ADR-0118 (2026-05-16)` header line in frontmatter or a 'Status' / 'Amendments' section.
findings.impact: Doc-style standard for amendment provenance is bypassed. Readers cannot tell from header that ADR-0104/0107 were modified post-acceptance; supersedes/amends chains in machine-readable decisions.json miss the amendment direction (ADR-0118 has supersedes=[ADR-0052] but no relation back from ADR-0104/0107).
findings.fix: Add `amended_by: [ADR-0118]` and `amended_on: [2026-05-16]` to ADR-0104 and ADR-0107 frontmatter, plus an 'Amendments' section at the end of each ADR body summarizing the inline edit and linking ADR-0118. Mirror in decisions.json.

findings.title: Tombstone retains old 'date: 2026-05-12' status line alongside new retirement metadata
findings.evidence: docs/governance-lanes/archive-orphan.md keeps `- status: Retired` and `- date: 2026-05-12` (original scaffold date) plus `- retired_on: 2026-05-16`. Reasonable but doc-style.md may prefer a single canonical status timestamp.
findings.impact: Cosmetic; could confuse readers about whether 2026-05-12 is still authoritative.
findings.fix: Optional: rename `date` field to `created_on` in tombstones to disambiguate.

what_is_missing: No update to docs/DOC-CATALOG.md adding ADR-0118 (and accumulated drift for ADR-0115/0116/0117)
No update to docs/ADR-INDEX.md adding ADR-0118
No update to docs/machine-readable/decisions.json adding ADR-0118 + supersedes link from ADR-0052 + reverse amendment links from ADR-0104/0107
No 'Amendments' section in ADR-0104 / ADR-0107 documenting the post-acceptance edit
No removal of the live archive-orphan row from the fitness lanes table (row stays with 'retired' cells instead of being moved to a 'Retired lanes' section, mixing live and retired lanes in one table)

ambiguity_risks.quote: The retirement keeps a small historical lane record at `docs/governance-lanes/archive-orphan.md` and `.omc/governance-lanes/archive-orphan.md` so IP-008 evidence remains explainable without keeping executable code.
ambiguity_risks.interpretation_a: Tombstone is the canonical retired-lane shape — future retirements follow this pattern.
ambiguity_risks.interpretation_b: One-off historical record for IP-008 only — no general retirement pattern established.
ambiguity_risks.risk_if_wrong: Without doc-style.md codifying the retired-lane tombstone schema, future retirements will diverge in fields, header, and INDEX placement.

multi_perspective_notes.stakeholder: Retirement decision is sound and ADR-0118 body is well-structured (id/status/deciders/supersedes/purpose all present). Failure is in the index/catalog hand-off, not in the decision itself.
multi_perspective_notes.executor: An agent searching DOC-CATALOG for 'archive-orphan' or ADR-0118 finds nothing — must already know the filename to locate the decision. Breaks the navigability invariant.
multi_perspective_notes.skeptic: PR #12 produced an identical A2 finding (ADR-0117 missing from indices). PR #13 repeats the exact pattern — the workflow has no enforcement coupling between adding an ADR file and updating the three indices. This is a systemic gap, not a one-off oversight.

principle_option_consistency: Pass — retirement aligns with no-sprawl (one-time lane removed) and Foundry pipeline canonicalization (ADR-0116).
verdict_justification: Three CRITICAL machine-readable index omissions plus one MAJOR amendment-annotation gap. Pattern matches A2 finding on PR #12 — systemic drift between ADR authoring and index maintenance. Realist check: doc-catalog and adr-index fitness lanes will mechanically flag this on next run, so impact is bounded — but the indices are the ONLY way agents discover decisions, so 'eventually flagged' does not save current readers. Severity stays CRITICAL.
open_questions: Does docs/standards/doc-style.md prescribe a retired-lane tombstone schema? If not, codifying one would prevent the next retirement from diverging.
Is there a script (e.g., scripts/regen-decisions-json.mjs) that regenerates decisions.json from ADR frontmatter? If so, was it run? If not, should it exist?
adversarial_reason: 3 CRITICAL findings exceeded the escalation threshold; reviewer hunted adjacent docs (DOC-CATALOG, ADR-INDEX, decisions.json) and confirmed systemic drift extending back to ADR-0115.
